newsitem.title: USA: US attacks IDA ban on purchases of American goods.
newsitem.headline: US attacks IDA ban on purchases of American goods.

text.p: The United States urged other donor nations on Monday to remove restrictions they have placed on the procurement of American goods by the World Bank's International Development Association.
"We ... urge donors ... to remove the procurement restrictions," Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin told the joint Development Committee of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
"These restrictions do not serve the interests of IDA's borrowers, nor do they provide incentive for continued U.S. participation," he added.
The restrictions were placed on procurement of U.S. goods because the United States did not contribute to an interim trust fund set up to finance IDA this year.
U.S. lawmakers have sharply criticized the action and have threatened that future U.S. funding for IDA could be at risk if the restrictions are not removed.

"We fully understand the importance other donors attach to 'equitable burden sharing,'" Rubin said. "But they need to understand that these restrictions have been counterproductive and they seriously jeopardize our ongoing ability to contribute to IDA."
